standard_prerequisites.name: Boundary maps of a short exact sequence of complexes and exactness of the two-periodic complexes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Homology, the long exact cohomology sequence of a short exact sequence of complexes, used at proof lines 17149-17161
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the two isomorphisms alpha_0 and alpha_1 as composites of boundary maps, and their being isomorphisms from the exactness of the two complexes.

core_obligations: Identify the two maps alpha_0 : Q -> K and alpha_1 : Q -> K explicitly as composites of the boundary maps arising from the two short exact sequences of complexes, and note that exactness of the two complexes makes them isomorphisms (proof lines 17149-17161).

Set up the length bookkeeping: with k = length_R(K), a = length_R(I_phi) and b = length_R(I_psi), use exactness to get length_R(M) = a + b, length_R(M') = a + b, length_R(N) = a + b - k, length_R(Q) = k, and the analogous identities for the primed images (proof lines 17163-17173).

Rewrite the hypotheses on K and Q as factorisations: K inside K_phi = I_psi gives the exact sequences 0 -> alpha(I_psi) -> N -> I_psi -> 0 and 0 -> alpha(I_phi) -> N -> I_phi -> 0, and the vanishing of psi' and phi' on Q identifies Q with I_{phi'}/alpha(I_phi) and with I_{psi'}/alpha(I_psi), giving the concrete descriptions of alpha_0 and alpha_1 (proof lines 17175-17210).

Choose admissible sequences generating K, I_phi and I_psi together with elements mapping onto them under phi and psi, compare the two defining symbols of the determinants through the admissible-sequence characterisation, and read off the scalar det_kappa(alpha_0^{-1} o alpha_1) (proof lines 17212 onward).
proof_roadmap: Identify the two boundary isomorphisms concretely (proof lines 17149-17210).
Record the length bookkeeping that fixes the ranks of all the modules involved (proof lines 17163-17173).
Choose the admissible sequences with their preimages and compare the two determinant symbols to extract the scalar (proof lines 17212 onward).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of exact (2, 1)-periodic complexes of finite length modules over a local ring whose maps induce zero on both the kernel K and the cokernel Q, the lemma asserts that det_kappa(M, phi, psi) equals det_kappa(alpha_0^{-1} o alpha_1) times det_kappa(M', phi', psi'), where the two isomorphisms Q -> K come from the boundary maps of the two short exact sequences of complexes displayed in the statement (statement lines 17107-17139). The proof is a long and explicit computation rather than a formal manipulation: the author first identifies the two boundary maps concretely as composites through the intermediate quotients I_{phi'}/alpha(I_phi) and I_{psi'}/alpha(I_psi) (proof lines 17149-17210), then does a length bookkeeping with k = length(K), a = length(I_phi) and b = length(I_psi) showing length(M) = length(M') = a + b while length(N) = a + b - k and length(Q) = k (proof lines 17163-17173), and finally chooses admissible sequences generating K, I_phi and I_psi together with preimages under phi and psi, compares the two determinants through the characterisation by admissible sequences, and tracks the scalar obtained (proof lines 17212 onward). The author explicitly notes that an alternative enormous commutative diagram exists and chooses the admissible-sequence route instead, which is why the argument is a delicate bookkeeping computation. Coordinating the boundary maps with the admissible sequences and their preimages is not a routine exercise, so the claim is H3.
